To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The proposed model can be used for the prediction of absorption rates of refrigerants in oil.

(i) absorption of refrigerant in lubricant oil is well described by a model that accounts for the effect of the solute on the liquid density; (ii) the effect of solubility on the apparent diffusion coefficients is negligible; (iii) absorption is not affected by the surface tension; and (iv) the thermodynamic model for the interfacial equilibrium is adequate for refrigerant mixtures with low solubility in the liquid phase.
The model is adequate for predicting absorption of refrigerant in lubricant oil and can be used to predict the effect of lubricant on absorption in a refrigeration system.

the absorption of a pure refrigerant can be described in terms of a single diffusion coefficient, whereas the absorption of a refrigerant mixture is described in terms by two diffusion coefficients, one in the vapor phase and another in the liquid phase.
